clause: Effects operator panel + Argus diagnostics + dual-audience manual (cross-cutting obligation) [STU-FX-040]

scope.summary: Build the unified operator Effects panel (the GUI projection of the effect model): view/add/reorder/toggle/mask/edit-params for every StudioEffectStack entry across all families, with stable Argus author_ids + machine-readable panel state (active entry, stack order, GPU/adapter state). Wire Argus visual-diagnostic coverage of effect rendering, GPU-fallback state, and cross-backend equivalence; and the dual-audience UserManual coverage duty: the effect model, EVERY catalog family (blur/distort/noise/pixelate/render/sharpen/stylize/artistic/utility/workspaces/layer-fx/vector/adapter), GPU/adapter requirements, and failure/recovery states (EFFECT_GPU_UNAVAILABLE / EFFECT_ADAPTER_UNAVAILABLE) - no effect row is complete until its model command + GUI surface + Argus hook + manual entry exist.
proof_targets: Argus panel inspect + manual coverage-completeness + fallback-state surfacing
expected_tests: argus: Effects panel reachable stable author_ids; panel state queryable (active entry/order/GPU state); no focus steal
HBR-MAN-003: every shipped effect command_id has a manual entry (coverage-completeness)
test: GPU-fallback + adapter-unavailable states surfaced in panel + Argus
acceptance_criteria_original: unified Effects panel (all families) + Argus diagnostics + dual-audience manual covering every family + GPU/adapter + failure/recovery; coverage-completeness passes

spec_clauses.spec_clause_text: [STU-FX-040] Every effect/filter capability in 14.9 is a single primitive with two projections — the operator effect UI and the typed model/MCP command surface ([STU-DOC-004]) — and MUST satisfy the cross-cutting obligations once, without re-statement per row: full model visibility and steerability of the effect stack, its entries, parameters, masks, order, and results per 14.16; parallel-safe, attributable, recoverable effect authorship per 14.17-14.19; the headless/quiet law per 14.20 ([STU-FX-038]); Argus visual-diagnostic coverage of effect rendering, GPU-fallback state, and cross-backend equivalence per 14.16/14.24; and dual-audience UserManual documentation of the effect model, every catalog family, GPU/adapter requirements, and failure/recovery states per 14.22. No effect row is complete until its model command, its GUI surface, its Argus diagnostic hook, and its UserManual entry exist. --- ## 14.10 Design Systems, Components & Variables ## 14.10 Design Systems, Components & Variables This sub-section is the normative Studio feature set for design systems: reusable component definitions, variant sets, component properties, the instance override model, the design-token variable system with its collections and modes, the multi-property style registry, and the responsive layout contract (auto layout, constraints, layout grids). It is the deduped union of the source suites' design-system surfaces collapsed to one Studio primitive and one command family per shared capability ([STU-SECTION-003]). Every capability here operates on `StudioLayer` nodes inside the single unified `StudioDocument` ([STU-DOC-001]). ### 0. Baseline, supersession and disposition

[STU-MAN-001] DUAL-AUDIENCE ENTRY CONTRACT. Every Studio tool, command, panel, and workflow MUST have ONE UserManual entry with two layers of the same entry: (a) an operator layer — user-friendly, task-oriented, minimal technicality ("how do I crop", "how do I mask", "how do I set type on a path"), navigation path, expected result; and (b) a model layer — technically complete: `command_id`, typed inputs/outputs, `dry_run` availability, receipt shape, undo semantics, Argus `author_id` targets, proof/evidence path, failure modes, recovery. Both layers satisfy CX-982-003 and CX-982-004 (Flight Recorder/EventLedger linkage + HBR-INT-009 three-tier posture per entry).

implementation_notes.naming: Vendor product names are provenance only. Studio ships Handshake-native names per [STU-SECTION-003].
implementation_notes.database: SurrealDB with the EventLedger is the only durable authority. SQLite, libSQL, Turso and PostgreSQL are forbidden, including in tests and dev caches.
implementation_notes.engine_split: GPU, WGSL and compute live in the studio-engine crate behind its traits. handshake_core must never gain a GPU dependency.
implementation_notes.routing: Navigation extends the existing address and bus seams. No new router.
implementation_notes.worktree: Code paths resolve against the WP-KERNEL-012 worktree, never main.

validator_focus: Confirm every acceptance row traces to a sentence in the cited spec clause carried in implementation_notes. A row with no spec basis is a fabrication.
Reject any row still carrying proof_target_status REQUIRED: it has no proof of its own.
Reject scaffold-only proof: at least one proof command must drive the executable runtime rather than a fixture the implementer authored.
Where the contract touches numeric parameters, confirm hard and soft bounds are stored as separate values and an unknown bound is stored as unknown, never mirrored.

resource_privacy_obligation.rule: Resources this contract reads, derives, caches or exports stay inside the authenticated operator's scope. No cross-identity read path may be introduced.

patch_provenance.preserved: The original acceptance prose is kept verbatim at scope.acceptance_criteria_original. No clause, scope decision, path list or obligation from the original contract was removed.

complete_canonical_scope_basis.heading: ### 20. Model Steerability, GUI, Diagnostics & Manual Obligation
complete_canonical_scope_basis.verbatim: [STU-FX-040] Every effect/filter capability in 14.9 is a single primitive with two projections — the operator effect UI and the typed model/MCP command surface ([STU-DOC-004]) — and MUST satisfy the cross-cutting obligations once, without re-statement per row: full model visibility and steerability of the effect stack, its entries, parameters, masks, order, and results per 14.16; parallel-safe, attributable, recoverable effect authorship per 14.17-14.19; the headless/quiet law per 14.20 ([STU-FX-038]); Argus visual-diagnostic coverage of effect rendering, GPU-fallback state, and cross-backend equivalence per 14.16/14.24; and dual-audience UserManual documentation of the effect model, every catalog family, GPU/adapter requirements, and failure/recovery states per 14.22. No effect row is complete until its model command, its GUI surface, its Argus diagnostic hook, and its UserManual entry exist.

complete_canonical_scope_basis.heading: ## 14.22 Studio UserManual (Dual-Audience)
complete_canonical_scope_basis.verbatim: [STU-MAN-001] DUAL-AUDIENCE ENTRY CONTRACT. Every Studio tool, command, panel, and workflow MUST have ONE UserManual entry with two layers of the same entry: (a) an operator layer — user-friendly, task-oriented, minimal technicality ("how do I crop", "how do I mask", "how do I set type on a path"), navigation path, expected result; and (b) a model layer — technically complete: `command_id`, typed inputs/outputs, `dry_run` availability, receipt shape, undo semantics, Argus `author_id` targets, proof/evidence path, failure modes, recovery. Both layers satisfy CX-982-003 and CX-982-004 (Flight Recorder/EventLedger linkage + HBR-INT-009 three-tier posture per entry).

spec_clauses.spec_clause_text: [STU-FX-040] Every effect/filter capability in 14.9 is a single primitive with two projections — the operator effect UI and the typed model/MCP command surface ([STU-DOC-004]) — and MUST satisfy the cross-cutting obligations once, without re-statement per row: full model visibility and steerability of the effect stack, its entries, parameters, masks, order, and results per 14.16; parallel-safe, attributable, recoverable effect authorship per 14.17-14.19; the headless/quiet law per 14.20 ([STU-FX-038]); Argus visual-diagnostic coverage of effect rendering, GPU-fallback state, and cross-backend equivalence per 14.16/14.24; and dual-audience UserManual documentation of the effect model, every catalog family, GPU/adapter requirements, and failure/recovery states per 14.22. No effect row is complete until its model command, its GUI surface, its Argus diagnostic hook, and its UserManual entry exist. --- ## 14.10 Design Systems, Components & Variables ## 14.10 Design Systems, Components & Variables This sub-section is the normative Studio feature set for design systems: reusable component definitions, variant sets, component properties, the instance override model, the design-token variable system with its collections and modes, the multi-property style registry, and the responsive layout contract (auto layout, constraints, layout grids). It is the deduped union of the source suites' design-system surfaces collapsed to one Studio primitive and one command family per shared capability ([STU-SECTION-003]). Every capability here operates on `StudioLayer` nodes inside the single unified `StudioDocument` ([STU-DOC-001]). ### 0. Baseline, supersession and disposition

[STU-MAN-001] DUAL-AUDIENCE ENTRY CONTRACT. Every Studio tool, command, panel, and workflow MUST have ONE UserManual entry with two layers of the same entry: (a) an operator layer — user-friendly, task-oriented, minimal technicality ("how do I crop", "how do I mask", "how do I set type on a path"), navigation path, expected result; and (b) a model layer — technically complete: `command_id`, typed inputs/outputs, `dry_run` availability, receipt shape, undo semantics, Argus `author_id` targets, proof/evidence path, failure modes, recovery. Both layers satisfy CX-982-003 and CX-982-004 (Flight Recorder/EventLedger linkage + HBR-INT-009 three-tier posture per entry).

implementation_notes.naming: Vendor product names are provenance only. Studio ships Handshake-native names per [STU-SECTION-003].
implementation_notes.database: SurrealDB with the EventLedger is the only durable authority. SQLite, libSQL, Turso and PostgreSQL are forbidden, including in tests and dev caches.
implementation_notes.engine_split: GPU, WGSL and compute live in the studio-engine crate behind its traits. handshake_core must never gain a GPU dependency.
implementation_notes.routing: Navigation extends the existing address and bus seams. No new router.
implementation_notes.worktree: Code paths resolve against the WP-KERNEL-012 worktree, never main.
